objects.original: An ideal pre-call history law, two conditional probability kernels at one call, and a history-dependent conditional discrepancy budget.
objects.reconstructed: A probability measure mu, Markov kernels K and L, and an integrable real function epsilon bounding every measurable-event discrepancy almost everywhere.
objects.evidence: The declaration gives these objects as explicit parameters. K and L act on the same input law; the proof compares their output event probabilities. Identifying mu with a concrete ideal-history law is not asserted by this generic component.

domains.original: Measurable histories and one-call outputs of the capped adaptive construction.
domains.reconstructed: Arbitrary measurable spaces A and B with explicitly supplied probability measure and Markov kernels.
domains.evidence: No countability, Euclidean, Gaussian or regular-conditional-distribution construction is assumed. The general measurable-space statement directly accommodates a supplied history/output kernel representation without claiming to construct it.

quantifiers.original: At an accepted history, the conditional total-variation budget controls all output events; average under the ideal-history law and obtain a bound for every output event.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For mu-almost every x, simultaneously for all measurable s, the conditional event bound holds; the conclusion quantifies over every measurable t.
quantifiers.evidence: hbound is ordered as almost every x followed by every measurable s, so one common exceptional null set suffices. The proof fixes t and specializes that hypothesis. A total-variation bound at each history implies precisely this uniform eventwise property.

assumptions.original: A common ideal-history probability law, genuine conditional probability kernels, and a measurable integrable local error budget.
assumptions.reconstructed: IsProbabilityMeasure mu, IsMarkovKernel K and L, Integrable epsilon mu, and the stated almost-everywhere event bound.
assumptions.evidence: The embedded proof bounds each conditional event probability by one and proves its integrability. Choosing the empty event in hbound forces epsilon to be nonnegative on the accepted histories; a separate nonnegativity premise is therefore unnecessary. No measurability of a conditional-TV supremum is silently inferred.

conclusion.original: Immediately after the replaced call, the discrepancy is bounded by the ideal-history mean of the local error.
conclusion.reconstructed: For each measurable t, abs((K composed with mu).real t - (L composed with mu).real t) is at most integral epsilon dmu.
conclusion.evidence: happly expresses both composed probabilities as real integrals. integral_sub, abs_integral_le_integral_abs and integral_mono_ae give the exact mean bound. For probability measures, a bound on every event is the usual supremum-over-events total-variation bound; no alternative normalization is introduced.
